channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [8] Topological textures in polar materials
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Krishanu Roychowdhury, Sujit Das

Authors: Zijian Hong, Yu-Tsun Shao, He Tian, Krishanu Roychowdhury, Sujit Das

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Review on topological textures in ferroelectric materials, relevant to broader condensed matter.

Tags: #topologicalmaterials #ferroelectrics #review #electronicdevices

Abstract: Ferroelectric materials can host robust and diverse polarization textures. This Review examines their formation mechanisms, responses to external stimuli and potential applications in next-generation electronic devices.

item.title: [9] Visualization of the Zhang–Rice singlet, electronic molecules and Cooper pair formation in a cuprate superconductor
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Changqing Jin, Yayu Wang

Authors: Shusen Ye, Jianfa Zhao, Zhiheng Yao, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct visualization of Cooper pair formation in a paradigmatic cuprate superconductor.

Tags: #cuprate #unconventionalsuperconductivity #STM/STS #stronglycorrelated

Abstract: How individual doped holes turn into superconducting Cooper pairs as doping increases in unconventional superconductors is still not well understood. Now, this process is observed in a paradigmatic cuprate compound.
